difficulty_reason: The statement asserts that the bivariant class P'_p(E_2), respectively c'_p(E_2), constructed in the preceding local lemma does not depend on the choice of the closed subscheme X_1 complementary to X_2 (statement lines 9751-9756). The proof takes a second closed subscheme X'_1 satisfying the same two conditions, notes that X = (X_1 cap X'_1) union X_2 set theoretically, and therefore decomposes any cycle class alpha in CH_k(X) as i_*beta + i_{2,*}alpha_2 with beta supported on the intersection and alpha_2 on X_2; capping the two candidate classes with alpha then both reduces to P_p(E_2) cap alpha_2, or to c_p(E_2) cap alpha_2 in the other case, so the result is visibly independent of the chosen complementary piece, and the same reasoning applies after any base change (proof lines 9758-9771). The decomposition of a cycle class along a cover by two closed subschemes is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
